q: Under NSCP 2015, how far may an unsupported longitudinal column bar be from a bar that is held by a tie corner?
o: No more than 150 mm clear on each side
Any distance, if the tie spacing is met
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 425.7.2 Ties.3
n: Every corner bar and every alternate bar must sit in a tie corner (angle no more than 135°), and no unsupported bar may be more than 150 mm clear from a supported one. Otherwise crossties are needed.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place non-prestressed concrete cast against and permanently exposed to earth?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Concrete cast directly on soil, such as footing bottoms, gets 75 mm because the surface is rough and wet and the steel must be well protected. Formed surfaces exposed to earth or weather need less (40 to 50 mm).

q: Under NSCP 2015, what cover applies to bundled bars in concrete not cast against earth?
o: Always 75 mm, the same as for concrete cast against earth
Twice the diameter of the largest bar in the bundle
The smaller of the bundle's equivalent diameter and 50 mm
Always 20 mm, the same as for single interior bars
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members; Sec. 420.6.1.3.4
n: Sec. 420.6.1.3.4: the cover for a bundle is at least the smaller of its equivalent diameter (the diameter of one bar with the same total area) and 50 mm. Where cast against earth it is 75 mm.

q: Under NSCP 2015, which of these is one of the three limits on the vertical spacing of column ties?
o: The largest dimension of the column
The least dimension of the column
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 425.7.2 Ties.1
n: Tie spacing must not exceed the smallest of 16 longitudinal bar diameters, 48 tie diameters and the least dimension of the column.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum inside bend diameter applies to a standard hook on 40 mm to 58 mm bars?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard Hook Geometry for Deformed Bars in Tension
n: Bend diameters grow with bar size so large bars are not cracked by tight bends: 6db for 10 to 25 mm, 8db for 28 to 36 mm and 10db for 40 to 58 mm bars.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place prestressed slabs, joists and walls exposed to weather or in contact with ground?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.2 Cover for Cast-in-Place Prestressed Concrete Members
n: For cast-in-place prestressed members, weather-exposed slabs, joists and walls need 25 mm and other exposed members 40 mm. Prestressed concrete is kept almost crack-free, so it needs less cover than non-prestressed concrete (40 to 50 mm).

q: Why must reinforcing bars have enough development length or hooks?
o: So the bars do not rust inside the concrete
So the concrete around the bars sets faster
So bond can build up the full design stress in the bar
So the bars can be joined without any lap splice
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 425.4 Development of reinforcement
n: A bar can only be stressed as far as the concrete can grip it. Without enough embedment it pulls out before yielding, and the member loses both strength and ductility. Hooks shorten the length needed.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what extension is required on a 135° hook of a stirrup or tie?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Minimum Bend Diameter and Hook Geometry for Stirrups, Ties and Hoops
n: A 135° stirrup or tie hook needs a 6db extension of at least 75 mm, bent around the longitudinal bar. It anchors into the core and does not pop out when the cover spalls, which is why seismic hooks are 135°.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to the primary reinforcement of cast-in-place prestressed beams and columns not exposed to weather?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.2 Cover for Cast-in-Place Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Interior prestressed beams and columns need 40 mm to their primary reinforcement and 25 mm to their stirrups, ties and spirals.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place non-prestressed concrete exposed to weather or earth, with 16 mm bars and smaller?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Formed concrete exposed to weather or earth needs 40 mm for 16 mm bars and smaller and 50 mm for 20 to 58 mm bars. Larger bars get more cover because they are harder to protect.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what hook may a 25 mm stirrup or tie use?
o: Only a 180° hook with a 4db extension
A 90° hook with only a 4db extension
A 135° hook (6db, at least 75 mm) or a 90° hook (12db)
No hook at all, only a straight bar end
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Minimum Bend Diameter and Hook Geometry for Stirrups, Ties and Hoops
n: For 20 to 25 mm stirrups and ties, a 90° hook needs 12db extension and a 135° hook needs 6db (at least 75 mm). 180° hooks are not listed for these sizes.

q: Why does concrete cast against earth need more cover than concrete cast in forms and later exposed to earth?
o: It sets faster, so it has less time to bond with the bars
It is always unreinforced, so the cover is only for appearance
It carries less load, so it can use more concrete
Its surface is rough and uneven and it stays in contact with moist soil
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Concrete poured straight onto soil has no form to give a true surface, and soil may mix into its skin, so NSCP asks for 75 mm instead of 40 to 50 mm.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to the primary bars, stirrups, ties and spirals of cast-in-place non-prestressed beams and columns not exposed to weather?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Interior beams, columns, pedestals and tension ties get 40 mm, measured to the outermost steel, usually the stirrups or ties.

q: Under NSCP 2015, tie spacing may not exceed how many tie-bar diameters?
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 425.7.2 Ties.1
n: The limits are 16 longitudinal bar diameters, 48 tie diameters and the least column dimension, whichever is smallest. With 10 mm ties, 48 × 10 = 480 mm.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum inside bend diameter applies to a standard hook on 28 mm to 36 mm bars?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard Hook Geometry for Deformed Bars in Tension
n: 28 to 36 mm bars bend around at least 8db; smaller bars (10 to 25 mm) 6db and larger bars (40 to 58 mm) 10db.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place prestressed concrete cast against and permanently in contact with ground?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.2 Cover for Cast-in-Place Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Concrete cast against earth takes 75 mm whether it is prestressed or not.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum tie size applies to columns with 36 mm longitudinal bars or with bundled bars?
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 425.7.2 Ties.2
n: Ties must be at least 10 mm for longitudinal bars 32 mm and smaller, and at least 12 mm for 36 mm and larger bars or bundles.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what straight extension is required after a 90° standard hook on a main bar?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard Hook Geometry for Deformed Bars in Tension
n: A 90° standard hook on a longitudinal bar needs a 12db extension. A 180° hook needs only 4db (at least 65 mm) because the full turn anchors better.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place prestressed slabs, joists and walls not exposed to weather?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.2 Cover for Cast-in-Place Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Interior prestressed slabs, joists and walls need 20 mm, the same as non-prestressed ones with 36 mm bars and smaller.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place non-prestressed concrete exposed to weather or earth, with 20 mm to 58 mm bars?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Weather-exposed formed concrete takes 50 mm for bars 20 mm and larger and 40 mm for 16 mm bars and smaller.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what extension is required on a 90° hook of a 20 mm or 25 mm stirrup?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Minimum Bend Diameter and Hook Geometry for Stirrups, Ties and Hoops
n: For 20 to 25 mm stirrups a 90° hook needs 12db. For 16 mm and smaller stirrups the same hook needs only 6db (at least 75 mm).

q: Under NSCP 2015, what applies to cover in corrosive environments or other severe exposure?
o: Cover may be reduced by 10 mm
Cover is increased as needed, or other protection is provided
No cover is needed if the bars are epoxy-coated
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members; Sec. 420.6.1.4
n: Sec. 420.6.1.4.1 lets the designer raise the cover in corrosive conditions, such as seawater splash zones, and requires the durability rules of Section 419.3 to be met, or other protection to be given.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place non-prestressed slabs, walls and joists not exposed to weather, with 36 mm bars and smaller?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Interior slabs, walls and joists need only 20 mm for 36 mm bars and smaller, and 40 mm for 40 to 58 mm bars.

q: A tied column has 20 mm longitudinal bars and 10 mm ties and measures 400 mm × 500 mm. What is the maximum tie spacing?
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 425.7.2 Ties.1
n: The spacing is the smallest of 16 × 20 = 320 mm, 48 × 10 = 480 mm and 400 mm, so 320 mm governs.
formula: s = min(16 db, 48 dtie, least column dimension)

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum inside bend diameter applies to a standard hook on 10 mm to 25 mm bars?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard Hook Geometry for Deformed Bars in Tension
n: Small and medium bars (10 to 25 mm) bend around at least 6db. Stirrups and ties of 16 mm and smaller may bend tighter, at 4db, because they are thinner.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum inside bend diameter applies to stirrups and ties of 16 mm and smaller?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Minimum Bend Diameter and Hook Geometry for Stirrups, Ties and Hoops
n: Stirrups and ties 16 mm and smaller bend around 4db. From 20 mm up they need 6db, the same as main bars.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum tie size applies to columns with longitudinal bars of 32 mm and smaller?
ref: NSCP 2015 Sec. 425.7.2 Ties.2
n: 10 mm ties are enough for longitudinal bars up to 32 mm. Bars of 36 mm and larger, or bundles, need 12 mm ties.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what straight extension is required after a 180° standard hook?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.1 Standard Hook Geometry for Deformed Bars in Tension
n: A 180° hook turns the bar fully back, so a short 4db tail is enough, but never less than 65 mm.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place prestressed members other than slabs, joists and walls, exposed to weather or in contact with ground?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.2 Cover for Cast-in-Place Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Exposed prestressed beams and columns need 40 mm; exposed prestressed slabs, joists and walls need 25 mm.

q: Where is concrete cover measured to?
o: The center of the main longitudinal bars
The outermost surface of the reinforcement, usually the stirrups or ties
The center of the member cross-section
The inside face of the main bars, toward the core
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members
n: Cover is the clear distance from the concrete surface to the nearest steel. In beams and columns that is usually the stirrup or tie, not the main bar behind it.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what extension is required on a 90° hook of a 16 mm or smaller stirrup?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 425.3.2 Minimum Bend Diameter and Hook Geometry for Stirrups, Ties and Hoops
n: Small stirrups (16 mm and smaller) with a 90° hook need 6db and at least 75 mm. Larger stirrups (20 to 25 mm) need 12db.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to the stirrups, ties and spirals of cast-in-place prestressed beams and columns not exposed to weather?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.2 Cover for Cast-in-Place Prestressed Concrete Members
n: In interior prestressed beams and columns, the primary reinforcement gets 40 mm and the stirrups, ties and spirals 25 mm.

q: Under NSCP 2015, what minimum concrete cover applies to cast-in-place non-prestressed slabs, walls and joists not exposed to weather, with 40 mm and 58 mm bars?
ref: NSCP 2015 Table 420.6.1.3.1 Cover for Cast-in-Place Non-Prestressed Concrete Members
n: The very large 40 and 58 mm bars need 40 mm even inside. Bars of 36 mm and smaller need only 20 mm.
